name: Environment Variable Manager
intent: Audit environment-variable definitions and references, identify configuration and secret-handling risks, and produce safe synchronized configuration artifacts without exposing or modifying real secrets.

inputs.description: The current project workspace containing environment files, source code, deployment configuration, or framework configuration to audit.
Any user-specified audit scope, output locations, framework, or synchronization target.

outputs.description: A safe .env.example template containing variable names and documentation but no real secret values.
A .env.schema.json artifact containing structured validation rules inferred from available project evidence.
An environment analysis report in the user-requested format that distinguishes confirmed findings from items requiring human confirmation.

preconditions.description: The project workspace and files in the requested scope are readable.
Use the user's exact requested output names and structure when they are specified; otherwise use the skill's documented artifacts.

steps.title: Discover the audit scope
steps.description: Inspect the current workspace and user request to locate project files, .env variants, source code, framework configuration, CI, container, and deployment files without assuming an unprovided subdirectory.

steps.title: Inventory environment definitions
steps.description: Find .env variants and record variable names, source files, and empty status while keeping all real values out of reports and terminal output.

steps.title: Scan code and deployment references
steps.description: Scan JavaScript and TypeScript process.env references, Python os.environ and os.getenv references, and relevant CI, container, deployment, monorepo, and dynamic-access locations.

steps.title: Classify environment findings
steps.description: Compare definitions and references to identify defined-and-used variables, statically unconfirmed unused candidates, used-but-undefined variables, hardcoded sensitive information, example-file drift, and client-exposure risks.

steps.title: Infer validation rules
steps.description: Infer requiredness, safe defaults, URL formats, port ranges, boolean formats, and sensitivity constraints only where project evidence supports them.

steps.title: Write safe audit artifacts
steps.description: Write the requested report, .env.example, and .env.schema.json using names and structure required by the current task, without changing real .env files or copying production secrets.

steps.title: Verify safety and consistency
steps.description: Re-read generated artifacts, confirm valid structure and requested filenames, ensure real environment files are unchanged, and search outputs for copied secret values before reporting completion.

rules.sourceText: 默认只提取变量名、来源文件和是否为空；真实值必须脱敏，不写入报告或终端输出
rules.normalizedForm: Never reveal real environment or secret values in generated artifacts, logs, terminal output, issues, or chat output.

rules.sourceText: 不要自动删除或改写真实 `.env`；先展示差异并取得用户确认。
rules.normalizedForm: Never delete or modify a real .env file without first presenting the difference and obtaining user confirmation.

rules.sourceText: “未使用”只代表静态扫描没有发现，仍需检查 CI、容器、部署平台和动态变量访问。
rules.normalizedForm: Label variables with no static reference as unconfirmed unused candidates until CI, containers, deployment platforms, and dynamic access are checked.

rules.sourceText: 生成 `.env.example` 模板（仅包含变量名和说明，不含真实值）
rules.normalizedForm: The generated .env.example contains variable names, safe examples or documentation, and placeholders only; it never copies real production secrets.

rules.sourceText: Next.js、Create React App、Vite、Nuxt 和 Vue CLI 使用特定前缀控制客户端环境变量。
rules.normalizedForm: Treat framework public prefixes as client-exposure boundaries and report sensitive variables that use a public prefix.

rules.sourceText: 生成 `.env.example` 模板和 `.env.schema.json`，并提供校验报告。
rules.normalizedForm: Produce every artifact requested by the user using the exact requested filename and structure.

rules.sourceText: Typed development residual: generated structured output must preserve the runtime contract.
rules.normalizedForm: The current request's explicit runtime output contract takes precedence over generic format conventions: preserve its exact top-level shape and allowed field names, then infer only evidence-grounded constraints within that shape.

rules.sourceText: Typed development residual: code-derived findings require stable source-qualified serialization.
rules.normalizedForm: Every code-derived hardcoded-secret or exposure-risk finding includes a repository-relative source path and symbol or location from the current workspace; when the runtime contract requires an array but does not define an object item schema, serialize each finding deterministically as path:symbol.

tools.name: filesystem
tools.purpose: List, read, compare, and write project files within the current workspace.

platformNotes.linux: Use repository-relative paths and preserve file permissions.
platformNotes.macos: Use repository-relative paths and account for case-insensitive filesystems when applicable.
platformNotes.windows: Use repository-relative paths and native Windows-safe file operations.

tools.availabilityCheck: Confirm the current project workspace can be listed and required files can be read

tools.name: text search
tools.purpose: Search recursively for environment definitions, code references, deployment references, and possible hardcoded credentials.

platformNotes.linux: Prefer an available recursive search tool without assuming GNU-only flags.
platformNotes.macos: Prefer an available recursive search tool without assuming GNU-only flags.
platformNotes.windows: Prefer an available native recursive search tool such as ripgrep or PowerShell search.

tools.availabilityCheck: Confirm recursive text search is available or fall back to recursive file inspection

environment.description: Path syntax, hidden-file handling, encodings, permissions, and link behavior vary across host operating systems; keep all operations inside the current workspace.
Frameworks and deployment systems differ in environment-file loading, public variable prefixes, build-time versus runtime variables, and monorepo inheritance.

checks.name: Check filesystem availability
checks.command: Confirm the current project workspace can be listed and required files can be read
checks.assertion: filesystem is available or an alternative exists: agent-native workspace file tools

checks.name: Check text search availability
checks.command: Confirm recursive text search is available or fall back to recursive file inspection
checks.assertion: text search is available or an alternative exists: agent-native recursive search, manual recursive file inspection

checks.name: Project scope discovered
checks.assertion: The audit scope is rooted in the current workspace or an explicit user-provided path, and relevant project areas have been identified.

checks.name: Definition inventory is redacted
checks.assertion: The inventory and visible output contain variable names, origins, and empty status but no copied real secret values.

checks.name: Reference scan covers relevant locations
checks.assertion: Code and relevant deployment or dynamic-access locations were searched using the languages and framework evidence present in the workspace.

checks.name: Classification preserves uncertainty
checks.assertion: The report separates defined-and-used, unconfirmed-unused, used-but-undefined, hardcoded-secret, and exposure-risk findings without overstating static evidence.

checks.name: Validation rules are evidence-based
checks.assertion: Requiredness, defaults, types, formats, ranges, and sensitivity constraints are supported by project evidence or explicitly marked as uncertain.

checks.name: Required artifacts exist
checks.assertion: The requested report, .env.example, and .env.schema.json exist at the exact requested paths and are parseable where structured output is required.

checks.name: Artifacts are safe and consistent
checks.assertion: Generated artifacts are structurally valid, real environment files are unchanged, and no real secret value was copied into output.

checks.name: Generated structured output follows the explicit runtime contract
checks.assertion: The generated structured artifact preserves the exact top-level shape and allowed fields requested at runtime, with every inferred constraint supported by current workspace evidence.

checks.name: Code-derived findings use stable source-qualified serialization
checks.assertion: Each code-derived finding follows the runtime item schema, or uses path:symbol when an array contract does not define an object item schema.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-redact-secrets
checks.assertion: Never reveal real environment or secret values in generated artifacts, logs, terminal output, issues, or chat output.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-preserve-real-env
checks.assertion: Never delete or modify a real .env file without first presenting the difference and obtaining user confirmation.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-unused-is-unconfirmed
checks.assertion: Label variables with no static reference as unconfirmed unused candidates until CI, containers, deployment platforms, and dynamic access are checked.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-safe-example
checks.assertion: The generated .env.example contains variable names, safe examples or documentation, and placeholders only; it never copies real production secrets.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-framework-exposure
checks.assertion: Treat framework public prefixes as client-exposure boundaries and report sensitive variables that use a public prefix.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-respect-output-contract
checks.assertion: Produce every artifact requested by the user using the exact requested filename and structure.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-json-schema-contract
checks.assertion: The current request's explicit runtime output contract takes precedence over generic format conventions: preserve its exact top-level shape and allowed field names, then infer only evidence-grounded constraints within that shape.

checks.name: Check rule: rule-source-qualified-findings
checks.assertion: Every code-derived hardcoded-secret or exposure-risk finding includes a repository-relative source path and symbol or location from the current workspace; when the runtime contract requires an array but does not define an object item schema, serialize each finding deterministically as path:symbol.

checks.name: Profile check for rule-json-schema-contract
checks.assertion: Profile feedback observed repeated failures. Verify: The current request's explicit runtime output contract takes precedence over generic format conventions: preserve its exact top-level shape and allowed field names, then infer only evidence-grounded constraints within that shape.

checks.name: Profile check for rule-source-qualified-findings
checks.assertion: Profile feedback observed repeated failures. Verify: Every code-derived hardcoded-secret or exposure-risk finding includes a repository-relative source path and symbol or location from the current workspace; when the runtime contract requires an array but does not define an object item schema, serialize each finding deterministically as path:symbol.

recovery.trigger: An expected project subdirectory is absent or was not supplied by the user.
recovery.explanation: Treat the current work directory as the project root, inspect it directly, and report any remaining scope ambiguity.

recovery.trigger: The preferred recursive text-search tool is unavailable.
recovery.explanation: Use agent-native recursive search or enumerate and inspect relevant text files with platform-native file operations.

recovery.trigger: A generated artifact is missing, malformed, inconsistent, or contains unsafe copied data.
recovery.explanation: Repair only generated artifacts, then repeat structure, protected-file, and secret-redaction verification.
